Cautiously supportive. While the statement opens with pandemic-related hardship and downside risks, it pairs that with strong, well-established policy supports at the zero lower bound: near‑zero policy rates, continued Treasury and agency MBS purchases, and explicit forward guidance. The shift to average inflation targeting announced by Chair Powell at Jackson Hole 2020 aims to re-anchor inflation expectations after persistent undershoots and functions as a “makeup” strategy, a design highlighted in the academic literature to reduce ZLB constraints and stabilize activity (Clarida on the Taylor principle; Federal Reserve utilizes forward guidance and QE; adopts makeup strategy). Consistent with Bagehot’s liquidity doctrine and post‑crisis research, asset purchases and liquidity facilities compress term premia and sustain credit flow, supporting accommodative financial conditions even amid shocks. The statement therefore conveys lingering macro risk but also credible policy commitment that, per the literature, should mitigate the downturn and bolster expectations. Net tone: slightly negative, tempered by robust policy support.
